steps.action: Unauthorized administration: open Settings General and Users as a Legal Team Member
steps.expected: Redirected away; the users and invite APIs refuse
steps.actual: Settings General and Users redirected Nadia to /settings/profile. GET /api/v1/users answered 403; POST /api/v1/auth/invites answered 403.

steps.action: Update organization details: Organization name saves on Enter, Escape restores, leaving the field saves
steps.expected: Saved status; Escape restores the previous name before saving; values survive reload
steps.actual: Enter showed Saved and "DOC-029 admin-org Helix mu48uxvf" survived reload. Escape put the saved name back in the field and nothing new saved. Typing the original name and leaving the field showed Saved; after reload the name was the original "Helix Software Group" again.

steps.action: Logo: Upload a supported image; a rejected file shows an error and can be retried
steps.expected: PNG saves; unsupported type and oversize files are refused
steps.actual: A .txt file and a 300 KB PNG each showed "The change could not be saved. Try again." and left the logo unchanged. Retrying with a 1x1 PNG showed Saved, and after reload the logo was a PNG data URI displayed as an image beside Logo. The original empty logo was restored through PATCH /api/v1/org/general (200) because the pane has no remove control.

steps.action: Default timezone saves and survives reload; Default locale offers English (United States) only
steps.expected: Timezone saved; one locale option
steps.actual: Default timezone saved America/Toronto and kept it after reload. Default locale offered only ["English (United States)"]. The timezone was restored to Europe/London.

steps.action: Invite a colleague: Invite user with Display name, Email, and Role Legal team member
steps.expected: Role offers Legal team member and Administrator; Send invite adds an Invited row with Resend invite and Revoke invite; email arrives
steps.actual: Role radios were ["Legal team member","Administrator"]. After Send invite the row read Invited with actions ["Resend invite","Revoke invite"] and no role control. Mailpit received "Set your OpenLaw password" with a set-password link.

steps.action: Invalid address is rejected
steps.expected: No row is created for an invalid address
steps.actual: The dialog stayed open with the browser message "Please include an '@' in the email address. 'doc029-org-invalid-address' is missing an '@'." and no row was added. The same invite route refused a malformed address with 400.

steps.action: Re-invite the pending address with the same role
steps.expected: The invitation is resent; no duplicate row
steps.actual: The dialog closed, a new "Set your OpenLaw password" email arrived, and the table still had exactly 1 row for the address.

steps.action: Re-invite the pending address with a different role
steps.expected: Refused because the account already exists; no email
steps.actual: The dialog showed "This user already exists with a different role." and no email was sent.

steps.action: Invite an already activated account
steps.expected: Refused
steps.actual: The dialog showed "This user has already activated their account.".

steps.action: Resend invite from the pending row
steps.expected: A replacement link is emailed
steps.actual: The row showed Saved and a new "Set your OpenLaw password" email arrived. Its link is the latest one and is used for activation below.

steps.action: A magic-link sign-in alone does not activate the invited row
steps.expected: The colleague signs in; the row stays Invited with Resend invite and Revoke invite
steps.actual: The staff sign-in page sent "Sign in to OpenLaw". Opening the link signed the colleague in (landed on /; /api/v1/me 200). Daniel's Users table still showed the row as Invited with ["Resend invite","Revoke invite"] and no role control.

steps.action: Set a password from the latest invitation link; the row becomes Active
steps.expected: Password set; row Active with role control
steps.actual: "Password set" appeared and the colleague signed in with the new password. The row read Active with a role control and actions ["Legal team member","Sign out user","Archive"].

steps.action: The activated Legal team member checks their access
steps.expected: No administration: Users redirects and there is no Invite user
steps.actual: Settings Users redirected to /settings/profile; no Invite user control was offered.

steps.action: Revoke invite withdraws an unused invitation
steps.expected: The pending row is removed
steps.actual: The Invited row for Bryn disappeared after Revoke invite, and GET /api/v1/users no longer listed the address.

steps.action: Change a role: promote the colleague to Administrator; the change applies on their next action
steps.expected: Role control offers three roles; colleague gains administration without signing in again
steps.actual: The role menu offered ["Administrator","Legal team member","Business user"]. Choosing Administrator showed Saved and the reloaded row read Administrator. The colleague's existing session opened Settings Users on its next navigation without signing in again.

steps.action: Change the role back to Legal team member
steps.expected: The colleague loses administration on the next request
steps.actual: The row saved Legal team member. The colleague's same session got 403 from GET /api/v1/users on its next request.

steps.action: Promote a Portal-created Business User with no password: the row becomes Invited without a role control
steps.expected: Invited row; Resend invite emails a link; setting a password returns Active with role control
steps.actual: The Portal sign-in link created an Active Business user row with a role control. Inviting that address as a Legal team member was refused with "This user already exists with a different role.". Promoting it to Legal team member turned the row Invited with ["Resend invite","Revoke invite"] and no role control. Resend invite sent "Set your OpenLaw password"; after the password was set the row read Active with its role control back.

steps.action: Return the activated account to Business user, then promote again
steps.expected: An already activated account stays Active and keeps its role control
steps.actual: Returned to Business user the row stayed Active with a role control. Promoted again it stayed Active with its role control, as the article's "If it still reads Active" branch says. It was left as a Business user.

steps.action: Your own row has no Sign out user or Archive action; self-archive is refused
steps.expected: No row actions on Daniel's row; API refuses self archive
steps.actual: Daniel's own row had a role control and no Sign out user or Archive action (buttons: ["Administrator"]). A direct archive request for his own account was refused with 409: "You cannot archive yourself.".

steps.action: Sign out user ends the colleague's sessions; the account stays active and can sign in again
steps.expected: Colleague's next request needs sign-in; row Active; password sign-in works
steps.actual: The visible action label was "Sign out user". The colleague's session went from 200 to 401 on /api/v1/me and the app sent it to /auth/login. The row stayed Active, and a password sign-in worked again (200).

steps.action: Archiving does not bulk-reassign work: a Contract keeps its Owner
steps.expected: The archived person stays the Contract Owner until someone reassigns it
steps.actual: Created Contract 34 with the colleague as Legal Owner (prepared through the API; the check follows in the archive step).

steps.action: Archive the colleague: the row leaves the ordinary list, sessions end, sign-in is blocked
steps.expected: Row hidden; live session ends; password sign-in refused; Contract Owner unchanged
steps.actual: Archive removed the row from the ordinary list at once. The colleague's live session went from 200 to 401. A new password sign-in showed "This account has been archived.". Contract 34 still named the archived colleague as Legal Owner (archived: true); nothing was reassigned.

steps.action: Show archived, Restore, and ask the user to sign in again
steps.expected: Restored row Active; the revoked session stays revoked; a new sign-in works
steps.actual: With Show archived on, the row read Archived with a Restore action. Restore showed Saved and the row read Active. The old browser session still got 401; a fresh password sign-in got 200.
